result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers separate defaulting to annual from hiding the monthly price, and both get the numbers right ($7.50 a month, $65.89 saved, about 42%). B gives a clearer recommendation and spells out what the grey text risks: refunds, chargebacks, complaints, bad reviews and churn at renewal. It also proposes a test that tracks refunds and 90-day retention alongside conversion, while A tracks only refunds and says little about how the grey text affects trust or complaints. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers separate pre-selecting annual from hiding the monthly price, and both use correct figures ($7.50/mo, $65.89 saved, about 42%). A explains more fully what the grey text risks (refunds, chargebacks, bad reviews, churn at renewal). It also proposes measuring refunds and 90-day retention as well as conversion, while B tracks only refund requests. B's pricing block and pre-renewal reminder are strong, but its recommendation ('Partly') is less decisive and it says less about measurement.
